faq.heading: The things operators ask me first

items.q: Do we have to replace our CRM or TMS?
items.a: No — and I'd advise against it. Everything I build sits alongside the systems you already run and talks to them through APIs, webhooks or a read replica. Replacing a working system is a multi-year project; this is a matter of weeks.

items.q: How long before something is actually live?
items.a: A pilot workflow is typically in front of real customers within two to four weeks. Full integration and rollout across channels usually adds another four to eight, depending on how accessible your systems are.

items.q: Won't the AI just make things up?
items.a: That is the failure mode I design against first. Answers are retrieved from your own records and cited, the agent is constrained to say "I don't know" rather than guess, and anything outside its confidence threshold escalates to a human. I also build evaluation sets so accuracy is measured, not assumed.

items.q: Will it quote a price without me approving it?
items.a: Only if you want it to. By default the agent gathers everything needed and drafts the estimate, but pricing authority stays with your team — you approve before it goes out. Some clients later let it auto-send within guardrails, once they have seen the accuracy for themselves.

items.q: Can it handle Spanish as well as English?
items.a: Yes. Bilingual English–Spanish handling on phone, chat and documents is standard — it matters for customers and crews alike in most US markets. Other languages can be added as your customer base requires.

The audit call is free. Pilots are fixed-fee against a defined success metric, so you know the number before you commit. Full builds are scoped after the pilot, and ongoing monitoring and tuning is a monthly retainer.

about.heading: I'm Hassan Rao. I build AI for companies that move things.
about.subheading: Five years shipping production software. Four of them building the systems that logistics operations actually run on.
about.body_1: Most of my career has been spent inside logistics software — platforms that handle thousands of shipments a day, the carrier integrations that feed them, and the automation that stops operations teams re-typing the same data every morning. Not consulting about it from the outside. Building it, then keeping it running.
about.body_2: I also built and run an AI phone receptionist that answers real customer calls in a natural voice and only says things it can back up with the company's own documents. That is the same architecture behind the booking and dispatch agents I build for movers and couriers — which is why I am fairly blunt about what these systems can and cannot be trusted to do.
about.body_3: So when we talk about your operation, I won't need three weeks to learn what a survey is, why crew allocation falls apart in peak season, or what happens when a driver marks a delivery as failed. I've had to build around all of it.
about.body_4: I work with a small number of clients at a time — moving companies, courier networks and freight brokers. Every engagement starts with a free audit call and a fixed-fee pilot, because I would rather prove one workflow works than sell you a twelve-month roadmap.
